claims.statement: Professional guidance supports explicit reevaluation and recontact policies and suitable informatics, but frames recontact as consent-aware, resource-constrained shared responsibility rather than an automatic universal duty.
ClinVar is a usable versioned public change source, but its uncurated submissions and variant-level model require laboratory-controlled patient matching and professional review.

Current Polish standards create a concrete audit-trail and authorization workflow: genetic reports must contain laboratory interpretation and the identity and signature of an appropriately qualified authorizer, and supporting records must permit reconstruction.
A production system handling identifiable genomic records needs a documented GDPR legal basis and safeguards; diagnostic intended-purpose language may also make the software an IVDR device.
QIAGEN and Fabric already provide adjacent or overlapping interpretation, workflow, reporting, reanalysis, and integration capabilities, so a standalone alert feed lacks defensibility.

Observed reanalysis availability does not establish recurring software demand: the US survey found low estimated provider-request uptake and heterogeneous billing, while European guidance says economic evidence is absent.

The proposed 42-account wealth path and 4,000 to 10,000 PLN monthly price are planning assumptions, not validated market facts; the only located Polish lab-count evidence is conflicting and historical.

contrary_evidence: QIAGEN reports a mature, IVDR-certified interpretation platform with case and workflow management, while Fabric advertises reanalysis, reporting, and LIMS or EMR integration.
Most surveyed US laboratories already offered reanalysis, yet estimated provider-request uptake was usually low and billing approaches varied materially.
ESHG explicitly states that there was no economic evidence supporting or opposing systematic recontact strategies and emphasizes fixed healthcare budgets.
Polish law requires qualified professional authorization, so automation cannot remove the scarce clinical labor completely.
